 1 Jar  Bay’s Kitchen Mild Korma Stir-in Sauce 
 300ml Bay’s Kitchen Vegetable Stock  (3 Tbsp Stock & 300ml of boiling water)
 225g Block Paneer cheese, cut into 2cm cubes 
 1 Large Leek (green part), finely sliced 
 150g Spinach 
 100ml Coconut milk
 75g Ground almonds 
 3 Tsp Coconut oil 
 3cm Sized Piece of ginger, peeled, minced 
 1 Tsp Ground cardamom 
 Sea Salt  
 Step #1
 Heat 1 tsp of oil in a large deep sided frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the paneer cubes and fry for 5 mins turning regularly so each side is golden brown. Once cooked remove from the pan and place on kitchen paper. 
Step #2
 Add the remaining 2 tsp oil then the leek tops and ginger to the pan and cook for 5-6 minutes until soft adding a splash of water halfway through .
Step #3
 Add the cardamom then fry for another 30 seconds then add the Bay's Kitchen Mild Korma Stir-in Sauce and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the ground almonds and fry for 1 minute more to create a thick paste. 
Step #4
 Mix 3 tbsp Bay's Kitchen Vegetable Stock with 300ml boiled water. Add this stock into the korma and bring to a simmer then cook for 5 minutes until it has reduced a little. Throw the spinach in the pan and cook for 5 minutes stirring to wilt.
Step #5
 Stir in the coconut milk and the paneer then check for seasoning adding little salt if needed. Cook for 2 minutes. 
Step #6
 Garnish with coriander and serves with basmati rice.

Tomato & Basil Gnocchi 🍅🌿
Ingredients
• 1 Bag Of Potato Gnocchi. 
• 1 jar Bay’s Kitchen Tomato & Basil Sauce. 
• Olive Oil.
• 1 Red Pepper, diced.
• 20–30g grated Parmesan.
1. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the diced pepper and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened.

Follow the recipe below to make your own at home.🤗
Easy Ginger, Spinach & Chive Chicken Broth 🫚🍲
Ingredients
• 500ml Boiling Water.
• Bay’s Kitchen Low FODMAP Chicken Stock. 
• 2 Handfuls Of Baby Spinach.
• 2 Tsp Of Grated Ginger.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Chives, finely chopped.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped.
• A Squeeze Of Fresh Lemon Juice.
• Black Pepper.
• Salt.
Method
1. Dissolve Bay’s Kitchen Chicken Stock in 500ml of boiling water.
2. Pour the stock into a saucepan and add the ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Simmer for 5–8 minutes to allow the ginger to infuse the broth.
4. Add the two handfuls of baby spinach and cook for 1–2 minutes, until just wilted.
5. Stir in the chopped chives, parsley, lemon juice, black pepper and salt to taste.
6. Divide between mugs and enjoy your warming, flavourful broth!

 We’re rounding off National Curry Week with our much loved Korma Curry Sauce!💜 The perfect sauce to warm up those colder evenings, while keeping things full of flavour and colour!👏🏻
Follow the recipe below and save it for your next cosy, comforting meal! 👇
🥘 Simple Vegetarian Korma Curry
Ingredients:
• 1 Sweet Potato, peeled and cut into small cubes.
• 1 Red Pepper, sliced.
• 2 Large Handfuls of Green Beans, sliced. 
• 60g Tinned Lentils, drained and rinsed.
• 1 Tbsp of Olive Oil.
• 1 Jar Of Bay’s Kitchen Korma Curry Sauce. 
• Basmati Rice, to serve.
• Fresh Coriander, optional for garnish.
• Crushed Peanuts, optional for garnish.
• Gluten Free Naan Bread.
Method:
1. Cook the sweet potato: Boil or steam for about 8–10 minutes, until tender. 
2. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan.
3. Add pepper and cook for 3–4 minutes.
4. Add the green beans and sweet potato and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
5. Stir in the lentils and korma curry sauce.
6. Simmer gently for 5–8 minutes, until everything is hot and the vegetables are cooked.
7. Serve with basmati rice, gluten free naan bread. 
8. Garnish with coriander and crush peanuts if desired.

 National Curry Week continues! 🍛 And with the weekend just around the corner we have an easy and delicious recipe for you to try.
Don’t forget to save this recipe for later! ❤️
🌶️ Your Low-FODMAP Thai Red Curry.
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce.
• 300g Chicken Breast, sliced.
• Olive Oil.
• 5 Pak Choi Leaves.
• 2 Large Handfuls of Spinach.
• Fresh Coriander.
• A Handful of Roasted Peanuts, roughly crushed for garnish. 
• Rice, to serve.
Method
1. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan.
2. Add the chicken and cook for 5–7 minutes until lightly browned and almost cooked through.
3. Pour in the Bay’s Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce with the Pak Choi and Spinach. 
4. Stir and simmer for 5–7 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and the vegetables have softened. 
5. Serve over rice of your choice, sprinkle with crushed roasted peanuts and coriander.

 It’s National Curry Week!! 🍛🙌🏼 And of course we had to give our Thai Massaman Sauce a moment in the spotlight! ✨
Our Prawn & Pineapple Thai Massaman Curry is the perfect midweek meal now that the autumn weather is here. This curry is comforting and packed full of flavour. 🍤🍍🌶️
Save this recipe for your next curry night if you’re in need of a little inspiration! 
This recipe can also be found directly on our website.🫶🏼
Ingredients:
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce.
• 200g Raw King Prawns (fresh or frozen will work).
• 150g Pineapple, roughly chopped.
• 1 Small Sweet Potato (max 150g), scrubbed and roughly chopped.
• 1 Spring Onion, green tops only, roughly chopped.
• 25g Salted Peanuts, roughly chopped.
• 1 tbsp Fish Sauce.
• 1 tbsp Coconut Oil.
• Small bunch of Coriander, roughly chopped.
• Sea Salt and freshly cracked Black Pepper.
To Serve:
• ½ lime, cut into quarters.
• Rice or gluten free naan bread.
Method: 
1. Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.
2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.
4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.
5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.
Step 6. Delicious with rice or gluten free naan bread.

Tomato & Basil Gnocchi 🍅🌿
Ingredients
• 1 Bag Of Potato Gnocchi.

• 1 Red Pepper, diced.

Ingredients
• 500ml Boiling Water.
• Bay’s Kitchen Low FODMAP Chicken Stock. 
• 2 Handfuls Of Baby Spinach.
• 2 Tsp Of Grated Ginger.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Chives, finely chopped.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped.
• A Squeeze Of Fresh Lemon Juice.
• Black Pepper.
• Salt.
Method
1. Dissolve Bay’s Kitchen Chicken Stock in 500ml of boiling water.
2. Pour the stock into a saucepan and add the ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer.
3. Simmer for 5–8 minutes to allow the ginger to infuse the broth.
4. Add the two handfuls of baby spinach and cook for 1–2 minutes, until just wilted.
5. Stir in the chopped chives, parsley, lemon juice, black pepper and salt to taste.
6. Divide between mugs and enjoy your warming, flavourful broth!

🥘 Simple Vegetarian Korma Curry
Ingredients:
• 1 Sweet Potato, peeled and cut into small cubes.
• 1 Red Pepper, sliced.
• 2 Large Handfuls of Green Beans, sliced. 
• 60g Tinned Lentils, drained and rinsed.
• 1 Tbsp of Olive Oil.
• 1 Jar Of Bay’s Kitchen Korma Curry Sauce. 
• Basmati Rice, to serve.
• Fresh Coriander, optional for garnish.
• Crushed Peanuts, optional for garnish.
• Gluten Free Naan Bread.
Method:
1. Cook the sweet potato: Boil or steam for about 8–10 minutes, until tender. 
2. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan.
3. Add pepper and cook for 3–4 minutes.
4. Add the green beans and sweet potato and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
5. Stir in the lentils and korma curry sauce.
6. Simmer gently for 5–8 minutes, until everything is hot and the vegetables are cooked.
7. Serve with basmati rice, gluten free naan bread. 
8. Garnish with coriander and crush peanuts if desired.

 It’s National Curry Week!! 🍛🙌🏼 And of course we had to give our Thai Massaman Sauce a moment in the spotlight! ✨
Our Prawn & Pineapple Thai Massaman Curry is the perfect midweek meal now that the autumn weather is here. This curry is comforting and packed full of flavour. 🍤🍍🌶️
Save this recipe for your next curry night if you’re in need of a little inspiration! 
This recipe can also be found directly on our website.🫶🏼
Ingredients:
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce.
• 200g Raw King Prawns (fresh or frozen will work).
• 150g Pineapple, roughly chopped.
• 1 Small Sweet Potato (max 150g), scrubbed and roughly chopped.
• 1 Spring Onion, green tops only, roughly chopped.
• 25g Salted Peanuts, roughly chopped.
• 1 tbsp Fish Sauce.
• 1 tbsp Coconut Oil.
• Small bunch of Coriander, roughly chopped.
• Sea Salt and freshly cracked Black Pepper.
To Serve:
• ½ lime, cut into quarters.
• Rice or gluten free naan bread.
Method: 
1. Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.
2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.
4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.
5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.
Step 6. Delicious with rice or gluten free naan bread.

 1 Jar Bay’s Kitchen Spicy Arrabbiata Stir-in Sauce 
 500g Ground turkey, preferably dark meat
 1 x 400g Tin chopped tomatoes
 1 Large Sweet potatoes (600g), peeled and cut into 3/4-inch chunks
 1 Large Leek (green part), finely sliced 
 150ml Water 
 2 Spring onions (green part), finely sliced 
 1/2 Lime, juiced
 1 Heaped Tsp ground cumin
 1 Heaped Tsp sweet smoked paprika
 1 Heaped Tsp chilli powder
 1/4 Tsp Asafoetida powder
 Extra-virgin olive oil
 Coriander, chopped (optional)
 Sea salt 
 For the almond cream:
 100g Almonds (60 almonds)
 100ml Water 
 Sea salt 
 Step #1
 Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone liner.
Step #2
 Toss the sweet potato chunks with a little oil until well coated, then spread on the baking sheet in a single layer. Sprinkle with a good pinch of the sea salt. Roast for about 20 minutes or until softened, stirring a few times. Let cool.
Step #3
 While the potatoes are roasting, heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Once hot, add the leek then cook for 5 minutes until softened. 
Step #4
 Add the turkey then break up with a wooden spoon and continue to cook until the meat is cooked through and its moisture has evaporated, which should take about 15 minutes. Keep breaking the meat up as you go. 
Step #5
 Add the asafoetida, cumin, paprika, chilli powder and a big pinch of salt, stirring to coat and cook for 1 minute more.
Step #6
 Add the peppers, tomatoes and the Bay's Kitchen Arrabbiata Stir-in Sauce and a big pinch of salt; increase the heat to high and add 1/2 the bay's kitchen jar of water. Once the mixture comes to a boil, reduce the heat to medium and cook, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
Step #7
 Stir in the cooled sweet potatoes and add the lime juice then adjust the seasoning as needed. Cook for another 10 minutes to blend the flavour adding more water if needed.
Step #8
 Take the pan off the heat then make the almond cream, by adding the almonds and water to a food processor and blitzing to a cream consistency.
Step #9
 Serve in bowls with a dollop of cream, sliced spring onions and coriander.

7. Serve with basmati rice, gluten free naan bread. 
8. Garnish with coriander and crush peanuts if desired.

 It’s National Curry Week!! 🍛🙌🏼 And of course we had to give our Thai Massaman Sauce a moment in the spotlight! ✨
Our Prawn & Pineapple Thai Massaman Curry is the perfect midweek meal now that the autumn weather is here. This curry is comforting and packed full of flavour. 🍤🍍🌶️
Save this recipe for your next curry night if you’re in need of a little inspiration! 
This recipe can also be found directly on our website.🫶🏼
Ingredients:
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce.
• 200g Raw King Prawns (fresh or frozen will work).
• 150g Pineapple, roughly chopped.
• 1 Small Sweet Potato (max 150g), scrubbed and roughly chopped.
• 1 Spring Onion, green tops only, roughly chopped.
• 25g Salted Peanuts, roughly chopped.
• 1 tbsp Fish Sauce.
• 1 tbsp Coconut Oil.
• Small bunch of Coriander, roughly chopped.
• Sea Salt and freshly cracked Black Pepper.
To Serve:
• ½ lime, cut into quarters.
• Rice or gluten free naan bread.
Method: 
1. Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.
2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.
4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.
5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.
Step 6. Delicious with rice or gluten free naan bread.

 It’s National Curry Week!! 🍛🙌🏼 And of course we had to give our Thai Massaman Sauce a moment in the spotlight! ✨
Our Prawn & Pineapple Thai Massaman Curry is the perfect midweek meal now that the autumn weather is here. This curry is comforting and packed full of flavour. 🍤🍍🌶️
Save this recipe for your next curry night if you’re in need of a little inspiration! 
This recipe can also be found directly on our website.🫶🏼
Ingredients:
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce.
• 200g Raw King Prawns (fresh or frozen will work).
• 150g Pineapple, roughly chopped.
• 1 Small Sweet Potato (max 150g), scrubbed and roughly chopped.
• 1 Spring Onion, green tops only, roughly chopped.
• 25g Salted Peanuts, roughly chopped.
• 1 tbsp Fish Sauce.
• 1 tbsp Coconut Oil.
• Small bunch of Coriander, roughly chopped.
• Sea Salt and freshly cracked Black Pepper.
To Serve:
• ½ lime, cut into quarters.
• Rice or gluten free naan bread.
Method: 
1. Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.
2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.
4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.
5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.
Step 6. Delicious with rice or gluten free naan bread.

 If possible, use a casserole dish / dutch oven to cook your biryani. If you don’t have one, use a deep, non-stick saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.

 Slice the spring onion tops, cut the pepper into bite size chunks and chop the coriander stalks and leaves, keeping them separate.
 Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces.
 Heat the oil in the pan and fry off the coriander stalks, spring onion tops, bay leaf and cardamom pods until fragrant.
 Add the chicken and fry until the meat is sealed on all sides.

7. Serve with basmati rice, gluten free naan bread.

4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.

Ingredients
• 500ml Boiling Water.
• Bay’s Kitchen Low FODMAP Chicken Stock. 
• 2 Handfuls Of Baby Spinach.
• 2 Tsp Of Grated Ginger.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Chives, finely chopped.
• 1 Tbsp Fresh Parsley, chopped.
• A Squeeze Of Fresh Lemon Juice.
• Black Pepper.
• Salt.
Method
1. Dissolve Bay’s Kitchen Chicken Stock in 500ml of boiling water.

4. Add the two handfuls of baby spinach and cook for 1–2 minutes, until just wilted.
5. Stir in the chopped chives, parsley, lemon juice, black pepper and salt to taste.
6. Divide between mugs and enjoy your warming, flavourful broth!

🥘 Simple Vegetarian Korma Curry
Ingredients:
• 1 Sweet Potato, peeled and cut into small cubes.
• 1 Red Pepper, sliced.
• 2 Large Handfuls of Green Beans, sliced. 
• 60g Tinned Lentils, drained and rinsed.
• 1 Tbsp of Olive Oil.
• 1 Jar Of Bay’s Kitchen Korma Curry Sauce. 
• Basmati Rice, to serve.
• Fresh Coriander, optional for garnish.
• Crushed Peanuts, optional for garnish.
• Gluten Free Naan Bread.
Method:
1. Cook the sweet potato: Boil or steam for about 8–10 minutes, until tender. 
2. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan.
3. Add pepper and cook for 3–4 minutes.
4. Add the green beans and sweet potato and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
5. Stir in the lentils and korma curry sauce.
6. Simmer gently for 5–8 minutes, until everything is hot and the vegetables are cooked.
7. Serve with basmati rice, gluten free naan bread. 
8. Garnish with coriander and crush peanuts if desired.

🌶️ Your Low-FODMAP Thai Red Curry.
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce.
• 300g Chicken Breast, sliced.
• Olive Oil.
• 5 Pak Choi Leaves.
• 2 Large Handfuls of Spinach.
• Fresh Coriander.
• A Handful of Roasted Peanuts, roughly crushed for garnish. 
• Rice, to serve.
Method
1. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan.
2. Add the chicken and cook for 5–7 minutes until lightly browned and almost cooked through.
3. Pour in the Bay’s Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce with the Pak Choi and Spinach. 
4. Stir and simmer for 5–7 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and the vegetables have softened. 
5. Serve over rice of your choice, sprinkle with crushed roasted peanuts and coriander.

 It’s National Curry Week!! 🍛🙌🏼 And of course we had to give our Thai Massaman Sauce a moment in the spotlight! ✨
Our Prawn & Pineapple Thai Massaman Curry is the perfect midweek meal now that the autumn weather is here. This curry is comforting and packed full of flavour. 🍤🍍🌶️
Save this recipe for your next curry night if you’re in need of a little inspiration! 
This recipe can also be found directly on our website.🫶🏼
Ingredients:
• 1 Jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce.
• 200g Raw King Prawns (fresh or frozen will work).
• 150g Pineapple, roughly chopped.
• 1 Small Sweet Potato (max 150g), scrubbed and roughly chopped.
• 1 Spring Onion, green tops only, roughly chopped.
• 25g Salted Peanuts, roughly chopped.
• 1 tbsp Fish Sauce.
• 1 tbsp Coconut Oil.
• Small bunch of Coriander, roughly chopped.
• Sea Salt and freshly cracked Black Pepper.
To Serve:
• ½ lime, cut into quarters.
• Rice or gluten free naan bread.
Method: 
1. Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.
2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.
4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.
5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.
Step 6. Delicious with rice or gluten free naan bread.
